rationale: Round 4 produced a genuine, specific new commitment from labour (good-faith negotiation on non-compulsory measures if a residual is verified) and sharpened the single remaining fault line—whether compulsory measures can ever re-enter the negotiable set after a genuinely exhausted, verified sequence—with State, Family Holding, and Investors now converging on pressing labour for symmetry on this point. This is a live, narrowing disagreement with clear movement across rounds, not a stalemate, so further rounds are likely to matter.
